articles.title: Welcome to Orca
articles.description: Learn how Orca organizes event planning work across your portfolio and event workspaces.
articles.bodyMarkdown:
Learn how Orca organizes event planning work across your portfolio and event workspaces.

## Overview

The account-level Command Center summarizes every event you can access. The Event Command Center summarizes one event.

An organization controls which events and administrative areas are available to you.

## When You’ll Use It

- Open this guide when you need to learn how Orca organizes event planning work across your portfolio and event workspaces.
- Use it during event setup and whenever a planner needs to recheck scope or navigation.

## Before You Begin

- You need an Orca account and access to the organization that owns the event.
- Gather the event dates, timezone, and any source material required by the task.

## Open Welcome to Orca

1. After sign-in, Orca opens the account-level **Command Center**.
2. Select an event from **Event Snapshot** or use **Search events** to enter its workspace.

## Orient Yourself

1. Open the account-level Command Center after sign-in.
2. Use the event list or event launcher to open an event.
3. Inside the event, use Roadmap, Budget, and Run of Show for the core planning work.
4. Use Directory, Attendees, and Speakers for people and program records.
5. Return to the Orca logo or account navigation when you need a portfolio view.

## Understand Important Concepts

- The account-level Command Center summarizes every event you can access. The Event Command Center summarizes one event.
- An organization controls which events and administrative areas are available to you.

## In-product Helper Text

> Command Center shows portfolio health. Open an event for detailed planning.

## Planner Tips

- Start a weekly review at the account level, then move into the event with the highest risk or nearest date.

## Best Practices

- Start portfolio reviews in the account Command Center; enter an event only when you need its detailed record.
- Do not use dashboard summaries as a substitute for updating Roadmap, Budget, Run of Show, Documents, or people records.

## Troubleshooting

### A control is missing or disabled

Confirm you have selected an organization, have access to the event, and completed every required field shown on the page.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Where is the system of record?

The selected organization and event determine scope. Once inside an event, the owning event module is authoritative.

Move between portfolio views, event workspaces, and event modules without losing context.

## Overview

Portfolio pages combine information across visible events. Event pages are scoped to the selected event.

Some direct-access pages are not listed in navigation; their documentation calls this out.

## When You’ll Use It

- Open this guide when you need to move between portfolio views, event workspaces, and event modules without losing context.
- Use it during event setup and whenever a planner needs to recheck scope or navigation.

## Before You Begin

- You need an Orca account and access to the organization that owns the event.
- Gather the event dates, timezone, and any source material required by the task.

## Open Navigate Orca

1. Use **Command Center**, **Portfolio Reports**, and **Settings** in the account sidebar.
2. Inside an event, use **Command Center**, the **Planning** section, and the **Management** section.
3. Select **Go to Command Center** to return to the account portfolio.

## Move Between Portfolio and Event Work

1. Use the account navigation for Command Center, Portfolio Reports, and Settings.
2. Select an event from the Command Center or event selector.
3. Use the event sidebar to open planning and people modules.
4. Use the event selector to move to another event while staying in the event workspace shell.

## Recognize Your Current Scope

1. Check the event name shown in the event workspace.
2. Confirm whether the page title says Command Center at account or event scope.
3. Before editing, confirm the event name and dates match the event you intend to update.

## Understand Important Concepts

- Portfolio pages combine information across visible events. Event pages are scoped to the selected event.
- Some direct-access pages are not listed in navigation; their documentation calls this out.

## In-product Helper Text

> Use the event selector to change events. Your current module remains visible when the destination supports it.

## Planner Tips

- Before a live planning meeting, open the correct event and module in advance to avoid editing a similarly named event.

## Best Practices

- Confirm the event name and dates before editing, especially when two events have similar names.
- Use the account Command Center for portfolio comparison and the event Command Center for one-event readiness.

## Troubleshooting

### A control is missing or disabled

Confirm you have selected an organization, have access to the event, and completed every required field shown on the page.

## Frequently Asked Questions

The selected organization and event determine scope. Once inside an event, the owning event module is authoritative.

Understand how organization context and event roles determine what you can see and change.

## Overview

Organization access determines the account and event set you can reach. Event-level roles can further limit editing.

Platform administration is reserved for SUPER\_ADMIN users and is not a normal planner workspace.

## When You’ll Use It

- Open this guide when you need to understand how organization context and event roles determine what you can see and change.
- Use it during event setup and whenever a planner needs to recheck scope or navigation.

## Before You Begin

- Open the correct organization and event.
- Confirm you have edit access before changing records.

## Open Organizations and Access

1. Sign in and check the organization name at the bottom of the account sidebar.
2. Open an event and confirm that its name and dates appear in the event selector.

## Check Your Organization Context

1. Sign in and open the account-level Command Center.
2. If Orca asks for an organization context, select the organization that owns the event.
3. Confirm the expected events appear before beginning work.

## Work With Event Permissions

1. Open an event you can access.
2. Viewers can read supported event pages but cannot change protected records.
3. Ask an organization administrator to adjust access when an edit control is unavailable for work you own.

## Understand Important Concepts

- Organization access determines the account and event set you can reach. Event-level roles can further limit editing.
- Platform administration is reserved for SUPER\_ADMIN users and is not a normal planner workspace.

## In-product Helper Text

> Read-only access lets you review event work without changing records.

## Planner Tips

- Use viewer access for stakeholders who need status visibility but should not change the planning record.

## Best Practices

- Give stakeholders Viewer access when they need visibility without editing rights.
- Resolve organization access before creating records; a duplicate event is not an access workaround.

## Troubleshooting

### I can see Orca but no events

Confirm that the correct organization is selected and that you have been granted access to an event in it.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Where is the system of record?

The selected organization and event determine scope. Once inside an event, the owning event module is authoritative.

Create an event workspace with the correct dates, timezone, and planning starting point.

## Overview

The builder creates one event workspace. Imported Run of Show, Budget, and Timeline records are scoped to that event.

Additional Docs accepts PDF, DOC/DOCX, JPG, and PNG files up to 50 MB each.

## When You’ll Use It

- Open this guide when you need to create an event workspace with the correct dates, timezone, and planning starting point.
- Use it during event setup and whenever a planner needs to recheck scope or navigation.

## Before You Begin

- You need an Orca account and access to the organization that owns the event.
- Gather the event dates, timezone, and any source material required by the task.

## Open Your First Event

1. From the account **Command Center**, select **Create Event**.
2. On **Create event workspace**, complete **Event details**, **Choose a starting point**, and **Review & create**.

## Enter Event Details

1. From the account-level Command Center, choose New Event.
2. Enter the Event name, Start date, End date, and Timezone.
3. Correct any validation message before continuing to Choose a starting point.

## Review and Create

1. Choose a starting point for the event.
2. Review detected records, issues, and mappings when your source contains planning data.
3. Add optional supporting documents if needed.
4. Choose the create action only after the event dates and import preview are correct.

- Additional Docs accepts PDF, DOC/DOCX, JPG, and PNG files up to 50 MB each.

> Event dates and timezone establish the calendar context for the workspace.

## Planner Tips

- Use the event venue timezone, not the planner's home-office timezone. Session times and onsite coordination depend on it.

## Best Practices

- Use the venue timezone and final contracted event dates before importing timed sessions.
- Review imported counts before inviting the wider team into the workspace.

Confirm you have selected an organization, have access to the event, and completed every required field shown on the page.

Choose between a template, spreadsheets, a pasted agenda, or an empty event workspace.

## Overview

Templates create starter sessions, a budget shell, and timeline tasks. They do not replace planner review.

A pasted agenda targets the Run of Show. Spreadsheet mapping can target Run of Show, Budget, and Timeline.

## When You’ll Use It

- Open this guide when you need to choose between a template, spreadsheets, a pasted agenda, or an empty event workspace.
- Use it during event setup and whenever a planner needs to recheck scope or navigation.

## Before You Begin

- You need an Orca account and access to the organization that owns the event.
- Gather the event dates, timezone, and any source material required by the task.

## Open an Event Builder Starting Point

1. Select **Create Event** from the account **Command Center**.
2. Complete **Event details**, select **Continue**, then choose **Upload Spreadsheet**, **Paste Agenda**, **Use Template**, or **Start Blank**.

## Choose a Source

1. Complete Event details and continue to Choose a starting point.
2. Choose a starter template for a Conference, Trade Show, Gala / Awards, Training, Workshop, or Corporate Meeting when you want a planning shell.
3. Choose spreadsheet import when Run of Show, Budget, or Timeline data already exists.
4. Choose the pasted-agenda option when your source is a rough text agenda.
5. Use an empty starting point when you want to build records manually.

## Understand Important Concepts

- Templates create starter sessions, a budget shell, and timeline tasks. They do not replace planner review.
- A pasted agenda targets the Run of Show. Spreadsheet mapping can target Run of Show, Budget, and Timeline.

## In-product Helper Text

> Starting points seed the workspace; you can continue editing every imported or template-created record.

## Planner Tips

- Choose the source with the most reliable structure. A clean budget workbook and a rough agenda can be handled separately after event creation.

## Best Practices

- Choose the structured source with the fewest cleanup exceptions.
- Use **Start Blank** only when no reliable agenda, workbook, or suitable template exists.

articles.title: Import Planning Spreadsheets
articles.description: Map existing workbook or CSV data into Run of Show, Budget, and Timeline records.
articles.bodyMarkdown:
Map existing workbook or CSV data into Run of Show, Budget, and Timeline records.

## Overview

Preview states include Ready, Needs review, and Skipped. A skipped row is not created.

Run of Show requires usable session timing; Budget and Timeline each have their own required fields.

## When You’ll Use It

- Open this guide when you need to map existing workbook or CSV data into Run of Show, Budget, and Timeline records.
- Use it during event setup and whenever a planner needs to recheck scope or navigation.

## Before You Begin

- You need an Orca account and access to the organization that owns the event.
- Gather the event dates, timezone, and any source material required by the task.

## Open Import Planning Spreadsheets

1. Select **Create Event**, complete **Event details**, and choose **Upload Spreadsheet**.
2. Upload `.xlsx` or `.csv` files, then continue to **Map spreadsheets**.

## Upload and Map Files

1. Choose spreadsheet import in the event builder.
2. Upload one or more readable .xlsx or .csv files.
3. Assign each relevant sheet to Run of Show, Budget, or Timeline.
4. Map required Planner fields to source columns. Leave irrelevant columns set to Do not map.

## Review the Import

1. Open Preview records, Issues, and Mapping.
2. Resolve missing required mappings and inspect skipped-row reasons.
3. Confirm the Will create totals for each module.
4. Continue to Review & create when the preview matches your source.

## Understand Important Concepts

- Preview states include Ready, Needs review, and Skipped. A skipped row is not created.
- Run of Show requires usable session timing; Budget and Timeline each have their own required fields.

## In-product Helper Text

> Required fields must be mapped before Orca can create records.

## Planner Tips

- Import the cleanest worksheet, not a presentation-formatted summary tab. Remove subtotal and decorative rows before upload when possible.

## Best Practices

- Remove subtotal, title, and decorative rows from source sheets before upload.
- Treat skipped-row counts as work to reconcile, not as a successful import total.

## Troubleshooting

### I cannot continue to Review & create

Map every required field and ensure at least one sheet targets Run of Show, Budget, or Timeline.

### Where is the system of record?

The selected organization and event determine scope. Once inside an event, the owning event module is authoritative.

## Overview

- Return to it during portfolio review before choosing which event or source record needs action.

- Select the organization whose event portfolio you need to review.
- Remember that portfolio values come from the event modules you can access.

## Open the Account Command Center

1. Select **Command Center** in the account sidebar.
2. Use the KPI links, **Timeline Overview**, **Upcoming Deadlines**, financial panels, and **Event Snapshot** to open source work.

## Review Portfolio Health

1. Open Command Center from the account navigation.
2. Review event health and upcoming-event signals.
3. Scan budget, timeline, registration, and speaker readiness information for exceptions.
4. Open the event or linked record that needs follow-up.

## Sort the Event Snapshot

- This is the account-level Command Center. It is different from the Event Command Center inside one event.

- Begin portfolio reviews with health sorting, then compare the nearest events against budget and timeline signals.

articles.bodyMarkdown:
Manage the display terminology inherited by events in your organization.

## Overview

Account **Settings** currently provides organization-wide **Event terminology** controls. You can change the display labels used for Agenda, Run of Show, Matrix, and Show Flow.

Member administration and external integration controls are not available on this page. Orca does not display inactive controls or link to an unfinished integrations page.

## Before You Begin

- Select the correct organization.
- Confirm that you are authorized to change organization defaults.
- Remember that an event can override these display labels in its own **Settings** page.

## Update Organization Terminology

1. Select **Settings** in the account sidebar.
2. In **Event terminology**, edit one or more display labels.
3. Select **Save terminology**.
4. Wait for the saved confirmation before navigating away.

These changes affect display terminology only. Routes, permissions, analytics, and stored records remain unchanged.

## Understand Event Overrides

Events inherit organization labels unless an event editor selects an event-specific override. Open the event and select **Settings** to inspect or change its inherited values.

## Planner Tips

- Agree on organization vocabulary before active program planning begins.
- Use event overrides sparingly so planners can recognize the same workspace across the portfolio.
- Do not expect organization member management or integration setup on this page; those workflows are not currently available here.

articles.bodyMarkdown:
Prepare the attendee-facing agenda in a dedicated Registration staging workspace.

## Overview

**Reg Agenda** owns staged attendee-facing agenda entries. You can import sessions designated **Official agenda** in Run of Show, upload a spreadsheet, or create entries manually.

The current adapter stores entries inside Orca. It does not publish to an external registration provider, and the interface reports external synchronization as unavailable rather than implying success.

## Before You Begin

- Confirm that approved attendee-facing sessions are marked **Official agenda** in Run of Show.
- Clean session titles, dates, times, rooms, descriptions, tracks, and speaker information before import.
- You need event editor access to create, edit, publish, unpublish, archive, or import entries.

## Import Official ShowOps Sessions

1. Open the event and select **Reg Agenda**.
2. Select **Import official ShowOps sessions**.
3. Review imported, updated, unchanged, archived, warning, and error counts.
4. Resolve validation warnings before publishing entries.

The import is idempotent: unchanged sessions are not duplicated, and changed sessions update the existing staged entry. If an imported session is later unmarked in Run of Show, the next import archives and unpublishes its staged entry.

## Import a Spreadsheet

1. Choose a CSV, XLS, or XLSX file.
2. Review the detected column mapping and preview rows.
3. Correct invalid rows or mapping problems.
4. Confirm the import.

Imports recognize common agenda column names and report duplicates instead of silently creating repeated entries. Files are limited to 1,000 rows.

## Create or Edit an Entry Manually

Use manual entry for attendee-facing content that does not originate in Run of Show. Enter the title, date, start and end times, and other available details, then save. Open an existing entry to edit its staged values.

## Publish and Unpublish

Publish makes a valid staged entry available to Registration Agenda consumers inside Orca. Unpublish returns it to draft without deleting it. Remove archives the staged entry after confirmation.

Review the preview's field mapping and row-level validation. Correct the source file, then preview it again before confirming.
